faq.q: What's the difference between A and AAAA records?
faq.a: A records map domains to IPv4 addresses (32-bit). AAAA records map to IPv6 addresses (128-bit). Both can coexist; browsers prefer IPv6 when available.

faq.q: What are MX records for?
faq.a: MX (Mail Exchanger) records specify which servers handle email for a domain. The priority value determines order — lower numbers are tried first.

faq.q: Why do DNS changes take time?
faq.a: DNS caching. Records have TTL (Time To Live) values telling caches how long to store them. Changes propagate as caches expire, typically within 24-48 hours.

seoContent.what: DOCX to HTML conversion extracts content from Microsoft Word documents and converts it to clean, semantic HTML. It preserves headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, and basic formatting.
seoContent.why: Word documents can't be displayed on the web directly. Converting to HTML enables publishing Word content online, importing into CMSes, or extracting text with formatting preserved.
seoContent.when: Use DOCX to HTML conversion when publishing Word documents online, importing content into a CMS, migrating documentation to web formats, or extracting formatted text from Word.

faq.q: Does this preserve all Word formatting?
faq.a: Basic formatting (bold, italic, headings, lists, tables) is preserved. Complex features like embedded objects, macros, or advanced layouts may not convert perfectly.

faq.q: Is my document uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. CipherKit processes DOCX files entirely in your browser using the mammoth.js library. Your document never leaves your device.

faq.q: Can I convert back to DOCX?
faq.a: HTML to DOCX conversion is more complex and requires server-side processing. CipherKit currently supports DOCX to HTML direction only.

seoContent.what: An epoch converter transforms Unix timestamps (seconds since Jan 1, 1970) to human-readable dates and vice versa. It handles both seconds and milliseconds formats and shows times in multiple timezones.
seoContent.why: Epoch timestamps are compact and timezone-independent but unreadable. When debugging logs, APIs, or JWTs, you need to convert these numbers to understand when events actually occurred.
seoContent.when: Use epoch conversion when debugging timestamps in logs or APIs, calculating JWT expiry times, working with database timestamp columns, or converting between date formats.

faq.q: Seconds vs milliseconds?
faq.a: Unix timestamps are traditionally seconds (10 digits). JavaScript uses milliseconds (13 digits). Divide by 1000 to convert ms to seconds.

faq.q: What timezone are epochs in?
faq.a: Epoch timestamps are always UTC — they represent absolute moments in time. Convert to local timezone only when displaying to users.

faq.q: What's the Year 2038 problem?
faq.a: 32-bit signed integers storing seconds overflow on Jan 19, 2038. Modern 64-bit systems are unaffected; the problem impacts legacy 32-bit systems.

seoContent.what: Gzip compression reduces file sizes using the DEFLATE algorithm, commonly used for HTTP compression and file archiving. Decompression restores the original data from gzip-compressed content.
seoContent.why: Gzip is the standard for HTTP content compression, reducing bandwidth and improving page load times. Developers need to compress assets and decompress received content for debugging.
seoContent.when: Use gzip when compressing assets for web delivery, decompressing HTTP responses for inspection, reducing file sizes for storage, or debugging gzip-encoded API responses.

faq.q: What's the typical compression ratio?
faq.a: Text compresses well — 60-80% reduction is common. Already-compressed formats (JPEG, PNG, MP3) see little benefit since they're already compressed.

faq.q: Is gzip the same as zip?
faq.a: Different but related. Gzip uses DEFLATE compression for single files. ZIP is a container format that can hold multiple files, often using DEFLATE internally.

faq.q: Is this safe for sensitive data?
faq.a: CipherKit compresses/decompresses entirely in your browser. Your data never leaves your device.

seoContent.what: A hash comparator checks whether two hash values match, detecting even single-character differences. It performs constant-time comparison to avoid timing attacks when comparing sensitive hashes.
seoContent.why: Hash verification is error-prone — hashes are long strings of similar characters. A comparator instantly confirms whether hashes match and highlights differences if they don't.
seoContent.when: Use hash comparison when verifying file integrity, comparing password hashes during testing, validating download checksums, or troubleshooting why hashes don't match.

faq.q: Why not just use string comparison?
faq.a: For security, hash comparison should be constant-time to prevent timing attacks. Also, visual comparison of 64+ character strings is error-prone.

faq.q: What if my hashes are different lengths?
faq.a: They're definitely different — no need to compare further. Different algorithms produce different lengths (MD5=32, SHA-256=64, SHA-512=128).

faq.q: Why would valid hashes not match?
faq.a: Common causes: different encoding (uppercase vs lowercase), extra whitespace, wrong algorithm, or the files are actually different.

seoContent.what: HEIC to JPG conversion transforms Apple's High Efficiency Image format into universally-compatible JPEG. HEIC offers better compression than JPEG but lacks universal support outside Apple devices.
seoContent.why: iPhone photos use HEIC by default, but many websites, applications, and non-Apple devices don't support it. Converting to JPEG ensures universal compatibility.
seoContent.when: Use HEIC to JPG conversion when uploading iPhone photos to websites, sharing images with non-Apple users, preparing photos for printing services, or using images in applications that don't support HEIC.

faq.q: What is HEIC?
faq.a: HEIC (High Efficiency Image Container) is Apple's image format using HEVC compression. It offers ~50% smaller files than JPEG at similar quality but has limited support outside Apple.

faq.q: Does conversion lose quality?
faq.a: Some quality loss is inevitable converting to lossy JPEG. CipherKit uses high-quality settings by default to minimize visible degradation.

faq.q: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. CipherKit converts entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your photos never leave your device.

seoContent.what: HEIC to PNG conversion transforms Apple's High Efficiency Image format into lossless PNG. Unlike JPEG conversion, PNG preserves full quality and supports transparency if present in the original.
seoContent.why: When you need maximum quality from iPhone photos or need to preserve any transparency data, PNG is the better target format. It's lossless but produces larger files than JPEG.
seoContent.when: Use HEIC to PNG when you need lossless quality, when the HEIC might contain transparency, when preparing images for editing, or when file size isn't a concern.

faq.q: PNG vs JPEG for HEIC conversion?
faq.a: PNG is lossless but larger. JPEG is smaller but loses quality. Use PNG for editing or when quality is paramount; JPEG for web/email sharing.

faq.q: Can HEIC contain transparency?
faq.a: Yes, HEIC supports alpha channels. Converting to PNG preserves transparency; converting to JPEG fills transparent areas with white.

faq.q: Is conversion processed locally?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit converts entirely in your browser. Your photos never leave your device.

seoContent.what: HEIC to WebP conversion transforms Apple's HEIC format into Google's WebP format. WebP offers excellent compression like HEIC but with much broader support across browsers and platforms.
seoContent.why: WebP is supported by all modern browsers while HEIC is mostly Apple-only. Converting HEIC to WebP gives you small file sizes with universal web compatibility.
seoContent.when: Use HEIC to WebP when preparing iPhone photos for web use, optimizing images for performance, or needing small files with broad compatibility.
useCases: Preparing iPhone photos for web publishing
Optimizing images for Core Web Vitals

faq.q: WebP vs JPEG for HEIC conversion?
faq.a: WebP offers 25-35% smaller files than JPEG at equivalent quality. All modern browsers support WebP. Use JPEG only for legacy compatibility.

faq.q: Does WebP support transparency?
faq.a: Yes. WebP supports alpha channels like PNG, making it suitable for images with transparency.

faq.q: Is this processed in my browser?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit converts entirely locally using the Canvas API. Your photos never leave your device.

seoContent.what: Hex encoding converts bytes or text into hexadecimal representation — each byte becomes two hex characters (00-FF). It's a readable way to represent binary data using only 0-9 and A-F.
seoContent.why: Binary data can't be displayed as text or transmitted through text-based protocols. Hex encoding makes bytes readable and safe for display, logging, and transmission.
seoContent.when: Use hex encoding when displaying binary data in logs, debugging network protocols, encoding bytes for text transmission, or inspecting raw byte values.

faq.q: Why does hex double the length?
faq.a: Each byte (8 bits, 0-255) requires exactly 2 hex digits (00-FF). Hex encoding always produces output twice the length of input bytes.

faq.q: Is hex encoding encryption?
faq.a: No. Hex encoding is just a different representation. Anyone can decode it instantly — it provides no security.

faq.q: What's the difference from Base64?
faq.a: Hex uses 16 symbols and doubles size. Base64 uses 64 symbols and increases size by ~33%. Base64 is more compact; hex is more readable for byte inspection.

seoContent.what: Hexadecimal to decimal conversion transforms base-16 numbers (0-9, A-F) into standard base-10 numbers. It reverses the decimal-to-hex conversion commonly needed in programming.
seoContent.why: Hex is used for memory addresses, color codes, and byte values, but calculations and user display often need decimal. Converting between bases is a common developer task.
seoContent.when: Use hex to decimal conversion when reading memory addresses, converting hex color values to decimal RGB, calculating byte values, or debugging hex output.
useCases: Hex color to decimal RGB values

faq.q: How do I convert manually?
faq.a: Multiply each digit by 16^position (right-to-left, starting at 0). For 'FF': F(15)×16¹ + F(15)×16⁰ = 240 + 15 = 255.

faq.q: What about negative hex numbers?
faq.a: Hex doesn't inherently represent negatives. Signed interpretation depends on context — 0xFF could be 255 (unsigned) or -1 (signed 8-bit).

faq.q: Are A-F case sensitive?
faq.a: No. 'FF', 'ff', and 'Ff' all equal 255. Hex digits A-F represent 10-15 regardless of case.

seoContent.what: HTML decoding converts HTML entities (< > & " etc.) back to their original characters (<, >, &, "). It reverses HTML encoding used to safely display special characters.
seoContent.why: When scraping web content or processing HTML data, you encounter encoded entities. Decoding reveals the actual text content for processing, display, or further use.
seoContent.when: Use HTML decoding when processing scraped web content, reading encoded API responses, converting HTML entities in database exports, or displaying user-entered HTML-encoded text.

faq.q: What are HTML entities?
faq.a: Named (&) or numeric (&) codes representing characters that have special meaning in HTML. They ensure characters display correctly instead of being interpreted as markup.

faq.q: Why would text be HTML-encoded?
faq.a: To prevent XSS attacks and ensure proper rendering. Characters like <, >, &, and quotes are encoded to stop browsers from interpreting them as HTML tags or attributes.

faq.q: Does this decode all entity types?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit decodes named entities (&), decimal entities (&), and hexadecimal entities (&) — all standard HTML entity formats.

seoContent.what: An HTML formatter beautifies minified or poorly-indented HTML by adding proper indentation, line breaks, and consistent spacing. It makes HTML documents readable and maintainable.
seoContent.why: Minified HTML is unreadable. Production builds often strip whitespace. A formatter restores structure for debugging, editing, code review, and understanding markup hierarchy.
seoContent.when: Use HTML formatting when debugging minified production HTML, reformatting legacy markup, preparing HTML for code review, or understanding complex nested structures.

faq.q: Does formatting change how HTML renders?
faq.a: Usually no. Extra whitespace between tags is typically ignored. However, whitespace inside text nodes and pre/code elements is preserved and may affect display.

faq.q: Can I minify HTML too?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit's formatter includes a minify option that removes unnecessary whitespace for production use.

faq.q: Does this validate HTML?
faq.a: The formatter catches some syntax errors during parsing. For comprehensive validation, use a dedicated HTML validator like W3C's.

seoContent.what: An HTTP header parser analyzes and explains HTTP request/response headers. It breaks down headers into readable components, explains their purposes, and identifies security headers and their configurations.
seoContent.why: HTTP headers control caching, security, content negotiation, and more. Understanding what headers mean helps debug issues, configure servers correctly, and implement security best practices.
seoContent.when: Use HTTP header parsing when debugging API responses, auditing security headers, understanding caching behavior, or diagnosing CORS and content-type issues.

faq.q: What are the most important security headers?
faq.a: Content-Security-Policy (XSS prevention), Strict-Transport-Security (force HTTPS), X-Frame-Options (clickjacking), X-Content-Type-Options (MIME sniffing).

faq.q: How do caching headers work?
faq.a: Cache-Control sets caching rules (max-age, no-cache). ETag/Last-Modified enable conditional requests. Vary specifies which request headers affect caching.

faq.q: What causes CORS errors?
faq.a: Missing or incorrect Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. The server must explicitly allow the requesting origin, or use * for public APIs.

seoContent.what: An image enhancer improves image quality by adjusting brightness, contrast, saturation, sharpness, and other parameters. It helps correct exposure issues and make images more visually appealing.
seoContent.why: Photos often need adjustment — underexposed shots, washed-out colors, or soft focus. Enhancement tools fix these issues without requiring professional photo editing software.
seoContent.when: Use image enhancement when correcting exposure issues, boosting colors for web display, sharpening slightly soft images, or preparing photos for publication.

faq.q: Does enhancement degrade quality?
faq.a: Some processing can introduce artifacts if pushed too far. CipherKit applies adjustments at high quality, but subtle corrections produce better results than extreme adjustments.

faq.q: Can I undo enhancements?
faq.a: CipherKit processes in real-time with live preview. Adjust sliders to undo changes. The original file isn't modified until you download the result.

faq.q: Is this processed locally?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit enhances images entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your photos never leave your device.

seoContent.what: An image resizer changes image dimensions by scaling, cropping, or fitting to specific sizes. It supports maintaining aspect ratio, setting exact dimensions, and choosing output quality.
seoContent.why: Images need resizing for web optimization, social media requirements, email attachments, or print specifications. Proper resizing ensures images fit their intended use without distortion.
seoContent.when: Use image resizing when preparing images for web upload, meeting platform size requirements, creating thumbnails, or reducing file size for email.

faq.q: Should I maintain aspect ratio?
faq.a: Usually yes. Changing aspect ratio distorts images. Maintain ratio and crop if needed to fit specific dimensions without stretching.

faq.q: Does resizing reduce quality?
faq.a: Downscaling is generally safe. Upscaling degrades quality since it must invent pixels. For best results, start with the largest source image available.

faq.q: What dimensions for web use?
faq.a: It depends on display size and density. For responsive images, provide multiple sizes. Maximum useful width is usually 2000-2500px for full-width images.

seoContent.what: IP address tools provide information about IP addresses: geolocation, ISP, hostname, subnet calculations, IPv4/IPv6 conversion, and network range analysis.
seoContent.why: Understanding IP addresses is essential for network administration, security analysis, and debugging connectivity. These tools reveal where IPs are located and what networks they belong to.
seoContent.when: Use IP tools when investigating suspicious traffic, debugging network connectivity, calculating subnet ranges, or understanding network architecture.

faq.q: How accurate is IP geolocation?
faq.a: Usually accurate to city level for most IPs. VPNs, proxies, and mobile networks can give misleading locations. It's not precise enough for exact addresses.

faq.q: What's the difference between IPv4 and IPv6?
faq.a: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses (4 billion possible). IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses (340 undecillion). IPv6 was created because IPv4 addresses ran out.

faq.q: What is CIDR notation?
faq.a: CIDR (like /24) indicates network size. /24 means 24 bits for network, 8 for hosts = 256 addresses. Lower numbers = larger networks.

seoContent.what: JPG to PNG conversion transforms lossy JPEG images into lossless PNG format. While this doesn't recover lost JPEG quality, it produces a lossless copy suitable for editing without further degradation.
seoContent.why: PNG doesn't degrade with repeated saves like JPEG does. Converting to PNG prevents further quality loss during editing workflows and supports transparency if you need to add it.
seoContent.when: Use JPG to PNG when preparing images for editing workflows, when you need to add transparency later, or when lossless format is required for specific purposes.

faq.q: Does this improve JPEG quality?
faq.a: No. JPEG compression is lossy and irreversible. Converting to PNG creates a lossless copy of already-degraded data — it prevents further loss but doesn't restore original quality.

faq.q: Why is PNG file larger?
faq.a: PNG is lossless compression; JPEG is lossy. Lossless always produces larger files for photos. The tradeoff is no further quality degradation.

faq.q: Can I add transparency after conversion?
faq.a: Yes. PNG supports alpha channels. After conversion, you can add transparency in image editing software.

seoContent.what: A JavaScript minifier removes whitespace, comments, and shortens variable names to reduce file size without changing functionality. Minified JS loads faster and reduces bandwidth.
seoContent.why: Smaller JavaScript files mean faster page loads and better Core Web Vitals scores. Minification is a standard production build step for web performance optimization.
seoContent.when: Use JS minification when preparing JavaScript for production deployment, optimizing page load performance, or reducing bundle sizes.

faq.q: What's the typical size reduction?
faq.a: Usually 30-60% reduction for well-commented code. The more comments and whitespace in the original, the greater the reduction.

faq.q: Can I still debug minified code?
faq.a: Use source maps. They map minified code back to original source, enabling debugging. Generate source maps during your build process.

faq.q: Is this the same as obfuscation?
faq.a: No. Minification preserves functionality while reducing size. Obfuscation intentionally makes code hard to understand for intellectual property protection.

seoContent.what: A JSON minifier removes all whitespace from JSON data, producing the most compact representation. This reduces file size and bandwidth without changing the data structure.
seoContent.why: Formatted JSON is larger due to indentation and line breaks. Minifying JSON reduces API payload sizes and improves transmission speed.
seoContent.when: Use JSON minification when preparing API payloads, reducing config file sizes, optimizing JSON stored in databases, or minimizing data transfer.

faq.q: Does minification change the data?
faq.a: No. Whitespace in JSON is purely for readability. Minification removes it without affecting the actual data structure or values.

faq.q: How much smaller is minified JSON?
faq.a: Depends on original formatting. Heavily indented JSON can be 30-50% smaller when minified. Single-line JSON sees minimal reduction.

faq.q: Should I always minify JSON?
faq.a: For production/transmission, yes. For config files humans edit, keep it formatted. Minify when size matters; format when readability matters.

seoContent.what: A JSON Schema validator checks whether JSON data conforms to a defined schema. It validates types, required fields, formats, patterns, and constraints, reporting exactly what doesn't match.
seoContent.why: JSON Schema ensures data integrity. Validating against a schema catches malformed data before it causes errors downstream, making APIs and configurations more robust.
seoContent.when: Use JSON Schema validation when testing API request/response formats, validating config files, ensuring data imports meet requirements, or debugging schema violations.

faq.q: What is JSON Schema?
faq.a: JSON Schema is a vocabulary for annotating and validating JSON documents. It defines structure, types, required fields, and constraints in a machine-readable format.

faq.q: Which schema version does this support?
faq.a: CipherKit supports JSON Schema draft-07, the most widely used version. Most schemas are compatible across draft versions.

faq.q: How do I create a schema?
faq.a: Define an object with 'type', 'properties', 'required', and constraint keywords. Start simple and add validations as needed. Many tools can generate schemas from example JSON.

seoContent.what: JSON to CSV conversion transforms JSON arrays of objects into comma-separated value format. Object keys become CSV headers, and values become row data, creating spreadsheet-compatible output.
seoContent.why: CSV is the universal format for spreadsheets and data import. Converting JSON to CSV enables opening API data in Excel, importing into databases, or sharing with non-technical users.
seoContent.when: Use JSON to CSV when exporting API data to spreadsheets, creating reports from JSON sources, importing data into legacy systems, or preparing data for analysis tools.

faq.q: What JSON structure works best?
faq.a: An array of objects with consistent keys. [{"name":"Alice","age":30}, {"name":"Bob","age":25}] converts cleanly. Nested objects are flattened or stringified.

faq.q: How are nested objects handled?
faq.a: Nested objects can be flattened (parent.child) or converted to JSON strings. Deep nesting may require preprocessing for clean CSV output.

faq.q: What about arrays in values?
faq.a: Array values are typically converted to delimited strings (comma-separated) or JSON strings within the CSV cell.

seoContent.what: JSON to YAML conversion transforms JSON data into YAML format. YAML's indentation-based syntax replaces JSON's braces and quotes, producing more human-readable configuration files.
seoContent.why: YAML is preferred for config files (Kubernetes, Docker, Ansible) because it's more readable and supports comments. Converting JSON to YAML enables using data in YAML-based tools.
seoContent.when: Use JSON to YAML when creating Kubernetes manifests from JSON, preparing Docker Compose files, configuring Ansible playbooks, or making config files more readable.

faq.q: Is YAML always more readable?
faq.a: For config files, usually yes. For deeply nested or data-heavy content, JSON's explicit structure can be clearer. YAML excels at flat or moderately nested configs.

faq.q: Does YAML support everything JSON does?
faq.a: YAML is a superset of JSON — any valid JSON is valid YAML. YAML adds features like comments, multi-line strings, and anchors that JSON lacks.

faq.q: Can I convert back to JSON?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit supports bidirectional conversion. Paste YAML to get equivalent JSON output.

seoContent.what: JSON to XML conversion transforms JSON data structures into XML format. Objects become elements, arrays become repeated elements, and values become element content or attributes.
seoContent.why: Some legacy systems, SOAP APIs, and enterprise tools require XML. Converting JSON to XML enables interoperability between modern JSON-based systems and XML-based infrastructure.
seoContent.when: Use JSON to XML when integrating with SOAP web services, working with legacy enterprise systems, generating XML feeds, or meeting XML format requirements.

faq.q: How are arrays converted?
faq.a: Array elements become repeated XML elements with the same tag name. [{"item":1},{"item":2}] becomes <item>1</item><item>2</item>.

faq.q: What about attributes vs elements?
faq.a: By default, JSON properties become child elements. Some converters support conventions like @attr to create attributes, but this varies by tool.

faq.q: Can I convert XML back to JSON?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit supports bidirectional conversion. Note that XML has features (attributes, namespaces) that don't map perfectly to JSON.

seoContent.what: A JWT builder creates JSON Web Tokens by assembling header, payload, and signature. You specify claims (sub, exp, iat, etc.), choose the algorithm, and provide a signing key to generate valid tokens.
seoContent.why: Testing authentication systems requires generating JWTs with specific claims. A builder lets developers create test tokens without writing signing code or setting up auth infrastructure.
seoContent.when: Use JWT builder when testing authentication flows, creating tokens for development environments, learning JWT structure, or generating tokens with specific claims for debugging.

faq.q: Is it safe to generate JWTs online?
faq.a: CipherKit generates JWTs entirely in your browser. Your secret key never leaves your device. For production secrets, this is safer than server-based tools.

faq.q: What's the difference between HS256 and RS256?
faq.a: HS256 uses a shared secret for signing and verification. RS256 uses asymmetric keys — private to sign, public to verify. RS256 is better when verifiers shouldn't have signing ability.

faq.q: Which claims should I include?
faq.a: Standard claims: sub (subject), exp (expiry), iat (issued at), iss (issuer). Add custom claims as needed. Always include exp to limit token lifetime.

seoContent.what: A JWT encoder takes header and payload JSON, encodes them to Base64URL, and creates a valid JWT structure. With a secret key, it also generates the signature for a complete, signed token.
seoContent.why: Understanding JWT structure requires seeing how headers and payloads become tokens. An encoder shows the encoding process and produces tokens for testing authentication systems.
seoContent.when: Use JWT encoding when learning JWT structure, creating test tokens, debugging encoding issues, or generating tokens from custom header/payload combinations.

faq.q: What's Base64URL encoding?
faq.a: Like Base64 but URL-safe: + becomes -, / becomes _, and padding (=) is removed. This ensures JWTs are safe in URLs without percent-encoding.

faq.q: Can I create unsigned JWTs?
faq.a: Technically yes (alg: none), but unsigned JWTs are insecure and rejected by most systems. Always sign JWTs with a secret or key pair.

faq.q: How do I verify my generated JWT?
faq.a: Use CipherKit's JWT decoder to parse the token and verify the structure. For signature verification, use the same key and algorithm used for signing.

seoContent.what: A Lorem Ipsum generator creates placeholder text in varying lengths — paragraphs, sentences, or words. This pseudo-Latin text fills layouts during design without distracting readers with meaningful content.
seoContent.why: Designers need realistic text volume without meaningful content that distracts from visual review. Lorem Ipsum fills space predictably, letting stakeholders focus on design rather than copywriting.
seoContent.when: Use Lorem Ipsum when creating mockups, building page layouts before content exists, testing responsive typography, or demonstrating designs to stakeholders.

faq.q: Why use Lorem Ipsum instead of real text?
faq.a: Real text distracts viewers from design evaluation. Lorem Ipsum provides realistic word patterns and lengths without readable meaning, keeping focus on layout and typography.

faq.q: Is Lorem Ipsum actually Latin?
faq.a: It's pseudo-Latin derived from Cicero's 'De Finibus' (45 BC), but scrambled and modified. Individual words aren't real Latin vocabulary.

faq.q: Are there alternatives to Lorem Ipsum?
faq.a: Yes — Hipster Ipsum, Bacon Ipsum, Corporate Ipsum, etc. CipherKit generates classic Lorem Ipsum, the industry standard.

seoContent.what: Markdown to PDF conversion renders Markdown source into a formatted PDF document. It processes headings, lists, code blocks, tables, and other Markdown features into printable output.
seoContent.why: Markdown is great for writing but not for printing or sharing with non-technical users. PDF conversion creates professional documents from Markdown source for distribution.
seoContent.when: Use Markdown to PDF when creating printable documentation, sharing formatted reports, generating PDF from README files, or producing deliverables from Markdown source.

faq.q: Does this support code syntax highlighting?
faq.a: Yes. Fenced code blocks with language identifiers are syntax-highlighted in the PDF output.

faq.q: Can I customize the PDF styling?
faq.a: CipherKit applies clean default styling. For custom styles, you'd export to HTML first and apply CSS, then convert to PDF.

faq.q: Is my Markdown processed locally?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit renders Markdown to PDF entirely in your browser using jsPDF and marked.js. Your content never leaves your device.

seoContent.what: A number base converter transforms numbers between different radixes: binary (base-2), octal (base-8), decimal (base-10), hexadecimal (base-16), and any custom base from 2 to 36.
seoContent.why: Different bases serve different purposes — binary for bit patterns, hex for bytes, octal for Unix permissions. Converting between them is essential for low-level programming and debugging.
seoContent.when: Use base conversion when working with memory addresses, understanding binary data, converting Unix permissions, debugging bit patterns, or learning number systems.
useCases: Converting between hex, decimal, and binary

faq.q: Why does programming use different bases?
faq.a: Each has advantages: binary shows individual bits, hex is compact for bytes (2 digits = 1 byte), octal maps to 3-bit groups (used in Unix permissions). Decimal is human-readable.

faq.q: What bases are supported?
faq.a: Any base from 2 to 36. Bases above 10 use letters: A=10 through Z=35. Common bases are 2 (binary), 8 (octal), 10 (decimal), 16 (hex).

faq.q: How do I convert manually?
faq.a: To convert to decimal: multiply each digit by base^position (right-to-left). To convert from decimal: repeatedly divide by target base, remainders form digits.

seoContent.what: A password strength checker analyzes passwords for entropy, common patterns, dictionary words, and known breaches. It estimates crack time and provides specific feedback for improvement.
seoContent.why: Users often think passwords are stronger than they are. A strength checker reveals vulnerabilities — dictionary words, predictable patterns, insufficient length — before attackers exploit them.
seoContent.when: Use password strength checking when creating new passwords, auditing existing passwords, educating users about security, or testing password policy enforcement.

faq.q: What makes a password strong?
faq.a: Length matters most. 16+ random characters are better than 8 complex characters. Avoid dictionary words, patterns (123, qwerty), and personal information.

faq.q: Is my password sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. CipherKit analyzes passwords entirely in your browser. Your password never leaves your device — safe to check sensitive passwords.

faq.q: Why is my 'complex' password weak?
faq.a: Common substitutions (p@ssw0rd), keyboard patterns (qwerty), and dictionary words with numbers are well-known to attackers and included in cracking dictionaries.

seoContent.what: PNG to JPG conversion transforms lossless PNG images into compressed JPEG format. This significantly reduces file size for photographs while losing the PNG transparency support.
seoContent.why: PNG files are often too large for web use, especially for photographs. Converting to JPEG dramatically reduces file size when lossless quality and transparency aren't needed.
seoContent.when: Use PNG to JPG when reducing file sizes for web upload, preparing images for email, removing transparency, or converting screenshots of photos.
useCases: Reducing image file sizes for web

faq.q: Will I lose quality?
faq.a: Yes, JPEG is lossy compression. CipherKit uses high-quality settings by default. For photographs, the quality loss is usually imperceptible while files shrink dramatically.

faq.q: What happens to transparency?
faq.a: JPEG doesn't support transparency. Transparent areas are filled with a background color (typically white). Keep PNG if you need transparency.

faq.q: When should I keep PNG?
faq.a: Keep PNG for graphics, logos, screenshots with text, or images needing transparency. Use JPEG for photographs where exact colors aren't critical.

seoContent.what: A random string generator creates strings of specified length using cryptographically secure randomness. You can choose character sets: alphanumeric, letters only, numbers, or custom characters.
seoContent.why: Random strings are needed for test data, unique identifiers, sample content, and non-security tokens. Cryptographic randomness ensures unpredictability even for non-secret uses.
seoContent.when: Use random string generation for creating test data, generating unique identifiers, producing sample content, or any scenario needing unpredictable strings.

faq.q: Is this suitable for passwords?
faq.a: Yes, but use the dedicated password generator which enforces security requirements. This tool is more flexible but requires you to choose secure parameters.

faq.q: How random is it?
faq.a: CipherKit uses Web Crypto API (crypto.getRandomValues) for cryptographically secure randomness. It's unpredictable enough for any application.

faq.q: What character sets are available?
faq.a: Alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), letters only, numbers only, hex digits, or custom character sets you define.

seoContent.what: RIPEMD-160 is a cryptographic hash function producing a 160-bit (40 hex character) digest. Developed in Europe as an alternative to NSA-designed SHA algorithms, it's used in Bitcoin and PGP.
seoContent.why: While SHA-256 is more common, RIPEMD-160 is still used in Bitcoin addresses and some cryptographic applications. Understanding different hash functions is valuable for security work.
seoContent.when: Use RIPEMD-160 when working with Bitcoin address generation, implementing systems requiring RIPEMD-160, or comparing hash algorithm outputs.

faq.q: Is RIPEMD-160 secure?
faq.a: For general hashing, SHA-256 is preferred. RIPEMD-160 has no known practical attacks but provides less security margin than SHA-256. It remains secure for its current uses.

faq.q: Why does Bitcoin use RIPEMD-160?
faq.a: Bitcoin addresses use RIPEMD-160(SHA-256(public_key)) — 'Hash160'. The shorter 160-bit output makes addresses more compact than full SHA-256 would.

faq.q: How does it compare to SHA-1?
faq.a: Both are 160-bit hashes, but SHA-1 is considered broken due to collision attacks. RIPEMD-160 has stronger collision resistance. Still, use SHA-256 for new systems.

seoContent.what: RSA encryption/decryption performs asymmetric cryptography using public/private key pairs. Public keys encrypt data that only the corresponding private key can decrypt, enabling secure communication without shared secrets.
seoContent.why: RSA enables secure communication with anyone who has your public key, without pre-sharing secrets. It's fundamental to HTTPS, SSH, PGP, and most secure communication systems.
seoContent.when: Use RSA encryption when sending secret data to someone whose public key you have, testing asymmetric encryption implementations, or learning public-key cryptography.

faq.q: What key size should I use?
faq.a: 2048 bits minimum, 4096 recommended for sensitive data. Larger keys are more secure but slower. 1024-bit keys are considered insecure.

faq.q: Can I encrypt large data?
faq.a: RSA can only encrypt data smaller than the key size. For large data, encrypt with a symmetric key (AES), then encrypt that key with RSA. This is hybrid encryption.

faq.q: Is this safe in a browser?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit uses Web Crypto API for RSA operations. Your private key never leaves your browser.

seoContent.what: SHA-1 (Secure Hash Algorithm 1) generates a 160-bit (40 hex character) hash from any input. Once widely used, SHA-1 is now deprecated for security purposes due to demonstrated collision attacks.
seoContent.why: Understanding SHA-1 matters because legacy systems still use it. While SHA-256 is the modern choice, you may encounter SHA-1 in older software, Git commits (though changing), and historical data.
seoContent.when: Use SHA-1 only for legacy system compatibility, Git commit hashes, or non-security checksums. For any security application, use SHA-256 or SHA-3.

faq.q: Is SHA-1 secure?
faq.a: No. Google demonstrated a practical SHA-1 collision in 2017 (SHAttered). SHA-1 should not be used for security — certificates, signatures, or password hashing. Use SHA-256.

faq.q: Why is SHA-1 still used?
faq.a: Legacy compatibility. Git uses SHA-1 for commit hashes (transitioning to SHA-256). Old systems may require SHA-1. For new systems, always use SHA-256 or stronger.

faq.q: What's a collision attack?
faq.a: Finding two different inputs that produce the same hash. Collisions let attackers substitute malicious data that matches a trusted hash. SHA-1 collisions are now feasible.

seoContent.what: SHA-3 (Secure Hash Algorithm 3) is the newest SHA standard, based on the Keccak algorithm. It uses a completely different construction (sponge function) than SHA-2, providing an alternative if SHA-2 were ever broken.
seoContent.why: SHA-3 provides algorithmic diversity. If a weakness were found in SHA-2's Merkle-Damgård construction, SHA-3's sponge construction offers a secure fallback. It's also used in Ethereum.
seoContent.when: Use SHA-3 when systems specifically require it (Ethereum uses Keccak-256), when you need algorithmic diversity from SHA-2, or for future-proofing cryptographic designs.

faq.q: Is SHA-3 better than SHA-256?
faq.a: Both are secure. SHA-3 uses a different construction (sponge vs Merkle-Damgård), providing diversity. SHA-256 is faster in software; SHA-3 resists length extension attacks naturally.

faq.q: What's Keccak vs SHA-3?
faq.a: Keccak won the SHA-3 competition but NIST made small parameter changes for the final SHA-3 standard. Ethereum uses original Keccak-256, not NIST SHA-3-256.

faq.q: Should I switch from SHA-256?
faq.a: Not necessarily. SHA-256 remains secure with no known weaknesses. SHA-3 provides an alternative if that changes. Use whichever your system requires.

seoContent.what: SHA-512 generates a 512-bit (128 hex character) hash using the SHA-2 family algorithm. It provides the largest digest size in standard SHA-2, offering maximum security margin.
seoContent.why: SHA-512 offers the highest security margin of the SHA-2 family and is actually faster than SHA-256 on 64-bit systems due to native 64-bit operations.
seoContent.when: Use SHA-512 when maximum security margin is needed, when working on 64-bit systems where it's faster, or when longer hash output is specifically required.
useCases: When longer hash output is required

faq.q: SHA-512 vs SHA-256?
faq.a: SHA-512 produces longer hashes (128 vs 64 hex chars) and is faster on 64-bit CPUs. SHA-256 is sufficient for all practical purposes; SHA-512 adds security margin.

faq.q: Why is SHA-512 faster on 64-bit?
faq.a: SHA-512 uses native 64-bit operations. On 64-bit CPUs, these are single instructions. SHA-256 uses 32-bit operations that don't benefit as much from 64-bit architecture.

faq.q: When should I use SHA-512?
faq.a: For new systems on 64-bit hardware where performance matters, SHA-512 is a good default. For broad compatibility and smaller hashes, SHA-256 works everywhere.

seoContent.what: SVG to PNG conversion rasterizes vector SVG graphics into bitmap PNG images at specified dimensions. Unlike SVG, PNG is a fixed-resolution image format supported everywhere.
seoContent.why: SVG is vector and scalable but not supported everywhere — email clients, some CMS platforms, and older software may reject SVG. PNG provides universal compatibility.
seoContent.when: Use SVG to PNG when preparing graphics for email, social media, or platforms that don't support SVG, creating favicons, or generating fixed-resolution versions of vector assets.
useCases: Creating social media images from SVG

faq.q: What resolution should I use?
faq.a: Export at the size you'll display. For retina/HiDPI, export at 2x dimensions. SVG can be converted to any size since it's vector — choose based on target display size.

faq.q: Is transparency preserved?
faq.a: Yes. PNG supports alpha channels. Transparent areas in your SVG remain transparent in the PNG output.

faq.q: Why convert vector to raster?
faq.a: Compatibility. SVG requires browser/app support. PNG works everywhere. Trade scalability for universal compatibility when needed.

seoContent.what: A word counter analyzes text to provide word count, character count (with/without spaces), sentence count, paragraph count, and estimated reading time.
seoContent.why: Writers need to meet word count requirements, optimize content length for SEO, or estimate reading time. A word counter provides instant metrics for any text.
seoContent.when: Use word counting when writing to a target length, checking essay/article word counts, estimating content reading time, or analyzing text composition.

faq.q: How is reading time calculated?
faq.a: Average adult reading speed is 200-250 words per minute. CipherKit uses 200 WPM for a conservative estimate.

faq.q: Are hyphenated words counted as one or two?
faq.a: Typically as one word. 'well-known' is counted as a single word. This matches standard word processing conventions.

faq.q: Does this count special characters?
faq.a: Character count includes all characters. Word count splits on whitespace and punctuation. Special characters between letters don't split words.

seoContent.what: An XML formatter beautifies minified or poorly-indented XML by adding proper indentation, line breaks, and consistent spacing. It makes XML documents readable and shows the element hierarchy clearly.
seoContent.why: Minified XML is unreadable. API responses and configuration files often come without formatting. A formatter reveals the structure for debugging, editing, and understanding.
seoContent.when: Use XML formatting when debugging SOAP responses, working with configuration files, analyzing RSS/Atom feeds, or inspecting any XML data.

faq.q: Does formatting change XML semantics?
faq.a: Whitespace between tags is generally insignificant. However, whitespace inside text content is preserved. Formatting won't change data meaning for standard XML.

faq.q: Can I minify XML too?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit's formatter includes a minify option that removes unnecessary whitespace for compact output.

faq.q: Does this validate XML?
faq.a: The formatter catches well-formedness errors (unclosed tags, invalid syntax). For full validation against schemas (XSD/DTD), use a dedicated XML validator.

seoContent.what: XML to JSON conversion transforms XML documents into JSON format. Elements become objects, attributes become properties (often prefixed with @), and text content becomes string values.
seoContent.why: Modern applications prefer JSON, but many legacy systems, SOAP services, and data sources use XML. Converting XML to JSON enables processing with JavaScript and modern APIs.
seoContent.when: Use XML to JSON when integrating legacy SOAP services, processing RSS/Atom feeds, importing XML data into modern applications, or converting configuration formats.
useCases: Importing XML data into modern apps

faq.q: How are attributes converted?
faq.a: Common conventions prefix attributes with @ (@id, @class). Some converters use separate 'attributes' objects. Check the output format for your specific needs.

faq.q: What about namespaces?
faq.a: XML namespaces add complexity. Simple converters ignore or flatten namespaces. Complex XML may require preprocessing or namespace-aware conversion.

faq.q: Can I convert JSON back to XML?
faq.a: Yes. CipherKit supports bidirectional conversion. Note that XML features like attributes, comments, and processing instructions may not round-trip perfectly.

seoContent.what: A YAML formatter standardizes YAML formatting with consistent indentation, proper alignment, and clean structure. It can also validate YAML syntax and catch common errors.
seoContent.why: YAML is whitespace-sensitive — inconsistent indentation breaks files. A formatter ensures consistent style across configuration files and catches syntax errors before deployment.
seoContent.when: Use YAML formatting when cleaning up configuration files, standardizing YAML style across a project, catching indentation errors, or preparing YAML for code review.

faq.q: Does formatting change YAML semantics?
faq.a: Correct formatting doesn't change meaning. The formatter standardizes indentation (spaces, not tabs) and alignment while preserving all data.

faq.q: What indentation does YAML use?
faq.a: YAML requires spaces, not tabs. Common conventions use 2 spaces per level. CipherKit formats with consistent 2-space indentation.

faq.q: Does this validate YAML?
faq.a: Yes. The formatter catches syntax errors like inconsistent indentation, invalid characters, and structural issues during parsing.

Let the tool detect the position and generate FEN automatically.

faq.q: Can I analyze chess.com and Lichess games in real time?
faq.a: Yes. Paste supported live game URLs to follow moves with an eval bar and engine lines. For best responsiveness, use API-backed tracking where available.

faq.q: How accurate is screenshot-to-FEN conversion?
faq.a: For clear 2D boards, accuracy is typically high. If a piece is misread, use the board editor to correct the position before running deeper engine analysis.

faq.q: Is this suitable for opening preparation?
faq.a: Yes for practical review and fast idea generation. For deep prep, combine this with longer engine runs and database checks to validate critical lines.
